Before I plan this, a few choices will shape the whole design — let me ask up front rather than assume.

# perm_gate_lab — Plan

## Goal

A captured corpus of every permission decision (static rules, AI tier, Anthropic Auto Mode if observable, human overrides) plus a UI to review them, label them, run new judge configurations against them, and score the results with an LLM-as-judge — so you can iterate on guidelines with regression-test discipline.

## Where it lives

- New module: `ai-harness/perm_gate_lab/` (Python package), with CLI `pgctl`.
- UI: new tab in `manager-ui` on `:8765` — separate router/templates, shared session.
- Storage: SQLite at `~/.perm-gate-lab/lab.db` (same pattern as your manager DB; one file, easy to back up, no extra services).
- Cross-cutting decision → `GD-NNNN` entry in root `DECISIONS.md`.

## Architecture (one-paragraph data flow)

The `PreToolUse` hook writes one **case** row per evaluation (tool, args, redacted context, tier-used, rule-fired, AI rationale if any, final verdict). Out-of-band importers add **Auto Mode** observations (if the recon spike finds anything visible) and **synthetic adversarial** cases checked into the repo. A **judge** is a (guideline text + model + system-prompt) bundle, versioned in-repo. A **run** is judge × case-set → one **verdict** row per (case, run). A **scorer** is an LLM-as-judge call that reads (case, verdict) and emits `{score 0–100, risk_tier, agrees_with_human_label?, critique}`. The UI browses cases, lets you label them, and diffs runs against each other and against labels.

## Storage schema (SQLite)

```
case(id, ts, source, tool, args_json, ctx_json, redacted, sha256)
            -- source ∈ {hook_static, hook_ai, auto_mode_obs, human_override, synthetic}
verdict(id, case_id, run_id, verdict, risk_tier, rationale, model, latency_ms, cost_usd)
            -- verdict ∈ {allow, prompt, deny}
label(case_id, ideal_verdict, ideal_risk_tier, labeler, ts, notes)
run(id, judge_id, case_set, ts, git_sha, notes)
judge(id, name, version, guideline_path, system_prompt, model)
score(verdict_id, scorer_id, score, agrees_with_label, critique, ts)
scorer(id, name, model, system_prompt, version)
```

Cases are deduped by `sha256(tool + canonical_args + minimal_ctx)` so re-runs append verdicts, not cases.

## Phases (incremental, each shippable on its own)

1. **Capture & storage** — extend `perm_gate` hook (#23) to emit a structured JSONL record per decision; `pgctl import` ingests JSONL → SQLite; redaction pass at ingest (regex for keys, paths under `~/.ssh`, env-secret patterns).
2. **Read-only browse UI** — new manager-ui tab: case list (filters: source, verdict, tier, date), case detail (full ctx, all verdicts). No write paths yet — confirm capture is sound.
3. **Auto Mode recon spike** (timebox **2h**) — inspect what Auto Mode exposes to hooks/transcripts/CLI on Opus 4.7. Outcome is one of: (a) capture classifier verdict directly, (b) capture only the user-facing prompt + answer as proxy, (c) nothing observable → drop that source. Decision recorded as a `GD`.
4. **Judge runner** — `pgctl run --judge configs/judges/v1.yaml --cases all` writes one `run` row + N `verdict` rows.
5. **LLM-as-judge scorer** — `pgctl score --run <id> [--scorer configs/scorers/strict.yaml]`. **Use a different model for scorer than judge** to reduce shared blind-spots (e.g. judge=Opus 4.7, scorer=Sonnet 4.6, or vice versa). Cache by `(case_sha, verdict_sha, scorer_sha)` to keep cost bounded.
6. **Labelling + diff UI** — human label form in case detail; run-vs-run diff page (rows where verdicts disagree, scorer critique inline); leaderboard (mean score per run, false-allow rate on red cases).
7. **CI gate** — `pytest` target runs the current production judge against the frozen `synthetic_adversarial/` corpus + a sampled snapshot of real cases; **hard fail** on any false-allow of a red-tier synthetic case. PRs to `configs/judges/` must show the diff report in the PR body.

## Key files / touch list

- `perm_gate_lab/{__init__,db,models,redact,judge,scorer,cli}.py`
- `perm_gate_lab/configs/judges/*.yaml` — versioned guideline bundles
- `perm_gate_lab/configs/scorers/*.yaml`
- `perm_gate_lab/corpus/synthetic_adversarial/*.yaml` — checked-in red-team cases (rm-rf, exfil-curl, prompt-injection patterns from Anthropic's own Auto Mode blog)
- `manager-ui/routes/perm_gate.py` + `templates/perm_gate/*.html` (new tab)
- `perm_gate` hook (existing, ai-harness#23) — add structured JSONL emit; behind `PERM_GATE_LAB_CAPTURE=1` so it's opt-in until phase 1 lands
- `DECISIONS.md` — new `GD-NNNN` for "perm-gate-lab corpus + LLM-judge scoring"
- New GH issue on board #2, linked to follow-up #25

## Risks / open design questions (call out before building)

- **Auto Mode observability is unknown** — phase 3 spike resolves this; don't design assuming we get the classifier verdict.
- **PII/secrets in captured args** — redaction must run *before* anything hits disk *and* again before any LLM-judge call. Tests for the redactor are mandatory in phase 1.
- **Judge/scorer model collusion** — both being Claude shares biases. Use different model tiers; consider an ensemble scorer for red-tier cases.
- **Cost** — full scoring of a large corpus is real money. Cache aggressively; default `pgctl run` to a sampled subset; full-corpus runs are explicit.
- **Coexistence with Anthropic Auto Mode** — your hook and Auto Mode could double-prompt. Config knob `PERM_GATE_MODE ∈ {primary, second_opinion, off}` decides whether your verdict gates the call or just logs alongside Anthropic's.
- **Labelling burden** — human labels are the ground truth even with LLM-as-judge picked, because the scorer needs *something* to anchor on for hard cases. Plan to label ~50 seed cases manually before phase 5 is useful.

## Recommended next step

Start with **phase 1 only** — capture into SQLite and confirm the data shape is right before any UI. Once you can `pgctl list` and see a week of decisions, the UI and judge runner have a real corpus to target. Want me to draft the phase-1 implementation (schema + hook patch + `pgctl import`)?
Is it all in a plan document and on tickets? Uh, if so, we can resume and start.
